lines: A sequencer that plays the notes you select on its keyboard, stepping through them in the order produced by repeatedly adding a step number and taking the remainder after dividing by a length
Switches that note into the set the sequencer plays, in the lowest of the three octaves, where C is -1V
Switches that note into the set the sequencer plays, in the middle octave, where C is 0V
Switches that note into the set the sequencer plays, in the highest of the three octaves, where C is 1V
Scales the length CV by -10 to +10 before it is added to the length setting
Sets the length, the number the running total is divided by to give the remainder; 0 to 33, and the number in the window is the length actually in use
Scales the step CV by -10 to +10 before it is added to the step setting
Sets the step, the number added to the running total on every clock; 0 to 33, and the number in the window is the step actually in use
Switches the length between a prime number chosen by the length setting, 0 giving 2 and 33 giving 139, and the length setting used as the number itself
Switches the step between a prime number chosen by the step setting, 0 giving 2 and 33 giving 139, and the step setting used as the number itself
Offsets the position in the cycle by a whole number from 0 to the current length, changing which of the selected notes the cycle starts on
A voltage that moves the length, scaled by the length attenuverter and added to the length setting, the total clamped to 0 to 167
A voltage that moves the step, scaled by the step attenuverter and added to the step setting, the total clamped to 0 to 167
A rising edge above 1V advances the sequence by one position and moves the output to the next note
A rising edge above 1V sends the sequence back to the start of its cycle
The note the sequencer is on, as 1V/octave pitch, held until the next clock, with 0V for the C of the middle octave
Note — the key of the note being played is lit
Note — the sequence repeats after a number of clocks equal to the length, and it visits the most notes when the length, the step and the number of selected notes are different primes
modulo.notes: Two params carry the maker's tooltip name 'Only Primes': index 41 is the length row and index 40 the step row, confirmed from paramPos, not from the enum order. Keyboard params are numbered upward from the lowest octave. The prime table is indexed after the CV sum is clamped to 0-167, so CV can drive a prime length as high as 997 while the knob alone reaches 139.

lines: A slime mould simulation: agents crawl across a 127 by 127 pixel grid leaving coloured trails, one step per clock pulse, with three stepped voltages taken from the picture
A rising edge advances the simulation one step, moving every agent forward, adding its colour to the pixel it lands on and turning it towards the strongest nearby trail
A rising edge clears the picture and creates a fresh set of agents at random positions, headings and colours
A rising edge displaces every agent by a random amount in each direction, scaled by the jitter force setting
Sets how far an agent can be displaced by a jitter pulse, 0 to 25 pixels; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets how far an agent can be displaced by a jitter pulse, -10V for none and +10V for 25 pixels, in place of the jitter force knob
Clears the picture and creates a fresh set of agents at random positions, headings and colours
Sets how many agents are created, 0 to 5000, read at the next reset; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets how many agents are created, -10V for none and +10V for 5000, read at the next reset, in place of the agent count knob
Sets the largest amount of red an agent can be given, 0 to 1, each agent taking a random fraction of it; read at the next reset, and a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets the largest amount of blue an agent can be given, 0 to 1, each agent taking a random fraction of it; read at the next reset, and a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets the largest amount of green an agent can be given, 0 to 1, each agent taking a random fraction of it; read at the next reset, and a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets the largest amount of red an agent can be given, -10V for none and +10V for the full amount, read at the next reset, in place of the red knob
Sets the largest amount of blue an agent can be given, -10V for none and +10V for the full amount, read at the next reset, in place of the blue knob
Sets the largest amount of green an agent can be given, -10V for none and +10V for the full amount, read at the next reset, in place of the green knob
Sets how much of each pixel's colour spreads into the eight pixels around it on every step, 0 to 1; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets how much of each pixel's colour spreads into the eight pixels around it, -10V for none and +10V for all of it, in place of the diffusion knob
Sets how much of a pixel's colour is kept after each step, 0 clearing it at once and 1 keeping all of it; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets how much of a pixel's colour is kept after each step, -10V clearing it at once and +10V keeping all of it, in place of the retainment knob
Sets the angle either side of an agent's heading at which it samples the trail, 0 to 90 degrees, which is also the angle it turns by; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets the angle either side of an agent's heading at which it samples the trail and turns, -10V for 0 degrees and +10V for 90 degrees, in place of the sensor angle knob
Sets how far ahead of an agent its three sample points are taken, 0 to 20 pixels; a cable in its CV input replaces this knob
Sets how far ahead of an agent its three sample points are taken, -10V for 0 and +10V for 20 pixels, in place of the sensor offset knob
A stepped 0-10V from the brightness of every pixel whose row or column number is a multiple of three, moving once per step, despite the manual naming -10V to +10V
A stepped 0-10V from the brightness of every pixel whose row or column number is a multiple of five but not of three, moving once per step, despite the manual naming -10V to +10V
A stepped 0-10V from the brightness of every pixel whose row or column number is a multiple of seven but not of three or five, moving once per step, despite the manual naming -10V to +10V
Note — the simulation advances at most 60 times a second; clock, reset and jitter edges arriving faster than that produce no step
Note — each of the three voltage outputs keeps only the fractional part of the brightness total it sums, so the values jump rather than drift
Note — an agent that crosses an edge of the grid reappears on the opposite edge
LoFiTV.notes: The README says the three modulation outputs run -10V to +10V. The code sums non-negative pixel brightness, keeps the fractional part and scales it by 10, so the range is 0-10V; the lines say so. The reset button (param 9) has no configParam and so no maker tooltip. The picture is drawn by one canvas widget with no clickable parts.
